A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Similarity-Dissimilarity Loss research. All 20 pages of v4 and 27 pages of v5, including appendices, are readable, and their equations, figures, tables, and relocated material support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V4 reports original image, AAPD text-classification, and MIMIC ICD-coding experiments in Tables 1, 2, 4, and 5.

after.justification: V5 retains these original experimental results in Tables 1, 3, 4, and 5, including the appendix evaluations.

M1.justification: The proposed loss, similarity and dissimilarity factors in Equations 13–17, encoders, and two-stage training procedure are unchanged. Section 2.7 and Appendix A expand the explanation; Equation 26 presents an alternative that is discussed but not adopted.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MS-COCO, PASCAL, NUS-WIDE, AAPD, and the same six MIMIC configurations. Table 6 adds comparisons on the existing MIMIC-III-Full task, without expanding the proposed method's dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: V5 Table 6 substantially expands the reported ICD-coding comparisons to CAML, MSATT-KG, MSMN, KEPTLongformer, standalone PLM-ICD, PLM-CA, CoRelation, GKI-ICD, MRR, and AKIL. The existing ALL, ANY, and MulSupCon comparisons remain. These additional cited comparisons do not establish that the baselines were rerun.

E3.justification: Dataset splits, metrics, encoders, training stages, and stated hyperparameters match between v4 Appendices B–D and v5 Appendices D–F. Table 6 adds prior-method scores without reporting a changed experimental protocol for the proposed method.

E4.justification: The relational case analysis and existing performance-dispersion analyses are retained. No new ablation, sensitivity, robustness, or error-analysis experiment is reported. Appendices A and C provide design and computational-cost arguments, without measured tests of the alternatives or efficiency claims.

E5.justification: The descriptive standard deviations across methods in Figures 2 and 3 are unchanged. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests; v5 introduces no new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: All original result-table values are retained. New Table 6 adds prior-method results on MIMIC-III-Full, while merely rounding the existing proposed-method scores. For example, it reports a micro-F1 tie with GKI-ICD at 62.3, but lower macro-AUC, 94.5 versus 96.2. These are added comparisons, not improved same-setting results.

T1.justification: The five original theorems and their proofs are retained, with proofs moved from Appendix A to B. V5 adds Equation 26 and mathematical arguments about temperature modulation and weighting properties. Its new Section 2.7 assertion that K_d<1 for R4 conflicts with the retained proof establishing K_d=1.

C1.justification: V5 adds an explicit state-of-the-art claim for MIMIC-III-Full, drops the introduction's explicit 'first' claim, and restricts the stated scope to inter-label relations. The central loss contribution remains unchanged; unification of single-label and multi-label losses was already claimed in v4 Section 2.4.

C2.justification: Section 2.7 and Appendices A and C substantially expand explanations of semantic weighting, noise suppression, temperature placement, penalty-function choice, and efficiency. V5 also qualifies comparisons with MRR and AKIL because of their additional inputs. Its limitations section replaces the concluding future-work proposal on nonlinear and learnable weights with an expanded account of low-label-cardinality limitations already discussed in v4.

D1.justification: V5 clarifies that its positive set matches ANY and that no additional encoder passes or parameters are introduced. The code link changes from the guangminghuang repository to an anonymous repository; accessibility cannot be established from the PDFs. Hardware and documented training configurations remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V5 adds Wang and Liu's contrastive-loss analysis and eight further ICD-method references supporting Table 6, extending its medical state-of-the-art positioning. The existing related-work discussion is largely retained. Removing the explicit priority claim and specifying inter-label scope also modestly refine its novelty positioning.

P1.justification: V5 reorganizes experiments and results into one main section, moves detailed image and AAPD discussion into Appendix G, rewrites the abstract and conclusion, and expands the explanatory sections. It adds an appendix contents page and ethics, reproducibility, limitations, and LLM-use statements.

P2.justification: The document is extensively reformatted, including the title and author block, running headers, section typography, and page flow. The AAPD table and Figure 3 move into the appendix, and Table 6 is added. Existing figures retain their graphical content, and existing result tables retain their values.

improvement.justification: V5 adds useful comparison context through Table 6 and improves navigation while retaining the original method and results. However, its added explanations introduce mathematical inconsistencies: Section 2.7 contradicts the retained R4 proof, and Appendix A.1 claims lost SupCon compatibility even though Equation 26 recovers SupCon when both factors equal one. The gains in context and organization coexist with weakened mathematical exposition, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
